about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Wholemeal Pikelets with Ricotta
recipes.summary: Small, fluffy wholemeal pikelets served with ricotta and sliced pear, lightly sweetened.
steps: Whisk the flour, honey, egg and milk into a thick, lump-free batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook 1 minute until golden.
Serve with ricotta, pear and a dusting of cinnamon.
notes: Food safety: cook the pikelets until set through, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Cold pikelets are good in lunchboxes.

recipes.title: Baked Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
recipes.summary: A tray of oats baked with apple, cinnamon and milk, cut into squares for the week.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 20 cm baking dish.
Mix the oats, apples, cinnamon, baking powder and half the walnuts in the dish.
Whisk the milk, egg, honey and butter, then pour over the oats.
Scatter with the remaining walnuts and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set and golden.
notes: Food safety: bake until the middle is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and reheats in the microwave.

recipes.title: Tropical Mango Oat Pots with Lime
recipes.summary: Creamy overnight oats soaked in coconut milk and layered with fresh mango, no added sugar.
steps: Stir the oats, coconut milk, yoghurt and vanilla together in a bowl.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until the oats are soft and thick.
Toss the mango with the lime juice.
Layer the oat mixture and mango in jars and top with coconut.
notes: Stir well before layering.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Bowl with Cucumber and Seeds
recipes.summary: A savoury, high-protein bowl of cottage cheese, crisp cucumber, cherry tomatoes and mixed seeds.
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into two bowls.
Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the oil and lemon juice until well coated.
Pile the vegetables over the cheese and finish with the seeds, dill and pepper.
notes: Serve with wholegrain crispbread.
Low in sugar and quick for busy mornings.

recipes.title: Quick Berry Jam on Toast
recipes.summary: A quick jam from frozen berries with no added sugar, spread over wholegrain toast.
steps: Simmer the berries in a small saucepan for 12 to 15 minutes until broken down and syrupy.
Mash roughly and stir in the lemon juice.
Cool for 10 minutes until thickened.
Toast the bread until golden, spread with ricotta and top with the jam.
notes: Store extra jam in a jar in the fridge for up to 10 days.
The berries give natural sweetness, so no sugar is needed.

recipes.title: Almond Meal Breakfast Pancakes
recipes.summary: Low-carb pancakes made with almond meal and eggs, with a squeeze of lemon and yoghurt.
steps: Whisk the almond meal, eggs, milk, baking powder and vanilla into a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and firm in the middle.
Serve with yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook until the pancakes are firm and set through, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keep the pancakes small because they are delicate to flip.

recipes.title: Spinach and Mushroom Egg Muffin Cups
recipes.summary: Baked egg cups with spinach, mushroom and feta, made in a muffin tin for easy grab-and-go breakfasts.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 12 hole muffin tin.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 4 minutes until golden, add the spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper, then divide the vegetables, feta and spring onion across the tin.
Pour in the egg mixture and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and set.
notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.title: Greek Yoghurt Bowl with Walnuts and Cinnamon
recipes.summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with toasted walnuts, apple and cinnamon, a quick bowl with no added sugar.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Spoon the yoghurt into bowls and top with apple and walnuts.
Dust with cinnamon and drizzle with the honey.
notes: Use unsweetened yoghurt to keep the sugar low.
Add a spoon of chia seeds for fibre.

recipes.title: Oat and Seed Porridge with Poached Pear
recipes.summary: A creamy, nutty porridge of oats and seeds topped with soft cinnamon pear.
steps: Simmer the pear with the cinnamon and water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Cook the oats, sunflower seeds and milk in a saucepan over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring until creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with the pear and pepitas.
notes: Use any plant milk for a dairy free bowl.
Poach extra pear and keep it in the fridge for 3 days.

recipes.title: Rosemary Roast Potatoes for Christmas
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged, fluffy roast potatoes with garlic and rosemary, parboiled and roughed up for maximum crunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and heat the oil in a roasting tray for 10 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until the edges are soft, then drain and shake to rough up the surfaces.
Tip the potatoes into the hot oil, turn to coat and roast for 30 minutes.
Turn them, add the garlic and rosemary and roast for 20 to 25 minutes more until deep golden and crisp.
notes: Roughing up the surface gives a crunchy crust.
Use a hot tray so the potatoes sizzle on contact.

recipes.title: Maple Roasted Carrots and Sweet Potato
recipes.summary: Sweet roasted root vegetables glazed with maple syrup, mustard and thyme.

items: 500 g sweet potato, cut into batons

steps: Heat the oven to 210°C and toss the vegetables with the oil, salt and thyme on a large tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once.
Mix the maple syrup and mustard, drizzle over and roast for 10 to 15 minutes more until caramelised and tender.
notes: Do not crowd the tray or they will steam.
Good on a roast dinner or cooked ahead and reheated.

recipes.title: Green Beans with Bacon and Almonds
recipes.summary: Garlicky green beans with crisp bacon and toasted almonds, a festive side that suits any roast.
steps: Cook the bacon in the oil in a large pan for 5 minutes until crisp and lift out.
Add the butter and beans and cook for 8 minutes until blistered and tender.
Add the almonds and cook for 3 minutes until golden, tossing often.
Return the bacon, add the vinegar and pepper and cook until the beans are glazed.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through to 75°C before serving.
Trim the beans the same length so they cook evenly.

recipes.title: Orange and Berry Sauce for the Christmas Table
recipes.summary: A tart, jewel-red sauce simmered with orange juice and berries, great with turkey and ham.
steps: Combine the berries, orange zest and juice, sugar, cinnamon and water in a saucepan.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the berries burst and the sauce thickens.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cool, as the sauce firms up as it cools.
notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in a clean jar in the fridge.
Stir through a spoon of horseradish for ham.

recipes.title: Longevity Noodles with Mushrooms for Lunar New Year
recipes.summary: Long, uncut noodles tossed with mushrooms and garlic chives for luck and long life.

items: 1 bunch garlic chives, cut into 5 cm lengths

steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water until just tender, then drain and rinse. Do not cut the noodles, for long life.
Stir-fry the mushrooms in the vegetable oil over high heat for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss in the noodles, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and chives and stir-fry for 2 minutes until hot.
Finish with the sesame oil.
notes: Leave the noodles long as they stand for long life.
Use vegetarian mushroom sauce in place of the oyster sauce if you prefer.

recipes.title: Garlic Stir Fried Greens for Lunar New Year
recipes.summary: Bright, glossy choy sum stir-fried with plenty of garlic and a splash of Shaoxing wine.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the bok choy and toss for 2 minutes.
Splash in the wine, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the stems are tender but still crisp.
Finish with the sesame oil.
notes: Cook in two batches if your wok is small.
Greens stand for prosperity at the Lunar New Year table.

recipes.title: Jeera Aloo Cumin Potatoes for Diwali
recipes.summary: Golden potatoes tossed with toasted cumin seeds, turmeric and fresh coriander.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oil, add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they sizzle.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander and chilli, then the potatoes and salt.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Finish with the lemon juice and coriander.
notes: Skip the chilli for a milder dish.
Serve warm with puri or flatbread.

recipes.title: Paneer and Pea Pulao for Diwali
recipes.summary: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with golden paneer, peas and whole spices.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it for 15 minutes.
Fry the paneer in 1 tbsp ghee for 4 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Heat the remaining ghee, add the whole spices and cumin and fry for 30 seconds, then cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the rice, water, salt and peas, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Fold in the paneer, rest for 5 minutes and scatter with coriander.
notes: Soaking the rice is not counted in the preparation time.
Serve with raita.

recipes.title: Eid Saffron Rice with Almonds and Sultanas
recipes.summary: Buttery rice scented with saffron and cardamom, scattered with toasted almonds and sultanas.
steps: Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp of hot water.
Toast the almonds in the butter for 2 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Add the rice and cardamom and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Drizzle over the saffron, rest for 5 minutes, fluff and fold in the sultanas and almonds.
notes: Rinse the rice first for separate grains.
A pinch of saffron goes a long way.

recipes.title: Sheer Khurma Eid Vermicelli Pudding
recipes.summary: A creamy, cardamom-scented milk pudding with fine vermicelli, pistachios and sultanas.
steps: Toast the vermicelli in the ghee over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden brown.
Pour in the milk, add the cardamom and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the vermicelli is tender and the milk reduced.
Stir in the sugar and sultanas and cook for 3 minutes more until slightly thickened.
Serve warm or chilled, topped with the nuts.
notes: The pudding thickens as it cools, so loosen with milk.
Serve warm on Eid morning.

recipes.title: Classic Sage and Onion Stuffing
recipes.summary: A moist bread stuffing with onion, celery and plenty of sage, baked until crisp on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a baking dish.
Cook the onions and celery in the butter for 8 minutes until soft.
Mix with the bread, sage, parsley and pepper in a large bowl.
Beat the egg with the stock and stir through until the bread is moist.
Spoon into a greased dish and bake for 35 minutes until golden and crisp on top.
notes: Food safety: bake until hot throughout at 75°C and the egg is cooked, particularly if cooked inside poultry.
Make the day before and bake just before serving.

recipes.title: Green Bean Casserole from Scratch
recipes.summary: Green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce topped with crisp fried onions, no tins needed.
steps: Blanch the beans in boiling water for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Cook the mushrooms in the butter for 8 minutes until golden, add the garlic, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and stock and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Toss the beans in the sauce and tip into a baking dish.
Fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, mix with the panko, scatter over the beans and bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden.
notes: Assemble ahead and bake just before serving.
Use gluten-free crumbs if needed.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Mash with Pecan Crumble
recipes.summary: Smooth, buttery sweet potato mash topped with a crunchy pecan and oat crumble.
steps: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very soft, then drain well.
Mash with half the butter, the milk, cinnamon and salt until smooth, then spread in a baking dish.
Rub the remaining butter into the pecans, oats and sugar and scatter on top.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until the crumble is golden and crisp.
notes: Make the mash a day ahead and add the crumble before baking.
Swap the pecans for walnuts.

recipes.title: Pan Juice Gravy for the Holiday Roast
recipes.summary: A rich, glossy gravy made from the roasting tray juices, stock and a splash of wine.

items: 1/4 cup pan drippings from the roast

steps: Pour the fat and juices from the roasting tray into a saucepan, leaving the dark sediment behind.
Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes until golden brown.
Whisk in the wine, then the stock, worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon, then season with pepper.
notes: Food safety: bring the gravy to a rolling boil and serve steaming hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Strain for a smooth finish.

recipes.title: Creamed Corn from Scratch
recipes.summary: Sweet corn simmered in cream and a little butter until thick, spooned alongside holiday roasts.
steps: Melt the butter and soften the shallot for 3 minutes.
Add the corn and flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and milk and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Crush a third of the corn with a spoon and season with nutmeg and pepper.
notes: Frozen corn works well, as long as it is thawed first.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Tomato and Cheese Scrolls
recipes.summary: Soft, golden scrolls with a tomato swirl and melted cheese, perfect for weekend brunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour and sugar, then stir in the milk and butter to form a soft dough, adding flour if sticky.
Roll out on a floured bench to a 30 x 40 cm rectangle.
Spread with the tomato paste and scatter with cheddar, then roll up from the long side and cut into 8 slices.
Place cut-side up on the tray and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and cooked through.
notes: Add a pinch of dried oregano to the paste.
Reheat in the oven to crisp up the next day.
